about: Known Blotato post errors. Each entry is matched against the errorMessage of a failed post: a case-insensitive 'contains' match on any string in matchAny, or a regular expression in matchRegex. Entries are checked top to bottom and the first match wins, so keep specific entries above general ones. Explanations and steps are paraphrased from the official Blotato Error Reference; do not add causes the docs do not state. An entry without 'links' links to the Error Reference. 'nextSteps' are for the support agent (shown on the card). 'customerSteps' are for the customer (used in the reply draft) and may only contain fixes the Error Reference gives. 'handledBySupport: true' means the official fix can only be done by support, so the draft says support is handling it. 'example' is a sample of the error text, used by the tests and the drafts review page. 'why' is the explanation for the agent; 'customerWhy' is the explanation used in the reply draft, written for the customer and limited to what the Error Reference states. 'customerAsk' is one plain sentence asking the customer for details (a sentence, not a list: a draft has at most one numbered list).
scope: Included: Error Reference rows that quote an actual error text and concern publishing a post (media, accounts, limits, platform rejections, scheduling). Left out on purpose: rows about visual/video generation, comments, messages, DM automations, source extraction, connecting accounts in the web app, and rows that describe a symptom or a label rather than an error text. The docs do not say which of these texts can appear in a failed post's errorMessage, so some entries may never match in practice.

entries.title: The video file's real format was not recognized
entries.why: Blotato did not recognize the container format inside the file. A file name ending in .mp4 does not prove the file really is an MP4.
nextSteps: Inspect the file's actual metadata (container and codecs) instead of trusting the file extension.
Export the video again as MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio. Renaming the extension does not change the format.
Check the exported file's dimensions, size, and duration against the destination platform's requirements.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Unsupported media format: mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2
customerSteps: Export the video again as an MP4 file. Renaming the file to .mp4 is not enough, because the format inside the file stays the same.
Check the exported file against the requirements of the platform you are posting to.
Then create the post again with the new file.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not recognize the format inside the video file. A file name ending in .mp4 does not guarantee the file really is an MP4.

entries.title: The media format is not supported for this destination
entries.why: Blotato reported the media format as unsupported. The docs describe this for MOV files: Blotato recognizes them, but handling differs by platform (LinkedIn converts non-MP4 video to MP4, Facebook accepts MP4 and MOV, other platforms may receive the file unchanged).
nextSteps: For the widest compatibility, export the video as MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio.
If the video is longer than 120 seconds, prepare it to match the destination platform before uploading, because automatic conversion will not run.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Unsupported media format (.mov)
customerSteps: Export the video as MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio, which is the most widely accepted format.
If the video is longer than 120 seconds, prepare it to match the platform before uploading, because it will not be converted automatically.
Then create the post again with the new file.
entries.customerWhy: The video's format is not supported for this post. MOV files in particular are handled differently by each platform: LinkedIn converts them to MP4, Facebook accepts MP4 and MOV, and other platforms may receive the file unchanged.

entries.title: The attached media type is not supported
entries.why: The error says the media attached to this post is a type that is not supported. It does not say which file or which rule was broken.
nextSteps: Check every file in the post's mediaUrls against the destination platform's media requirements (format, size, duration, dimensions).
For video, the docs recommend H.264 video with AAC audio in an MP4 container for the widest compatibility.
Open the failed request in Blotato Logs to see the full payload and error for this post.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.sourceNote: This wording is the example errorMessage in the Get Post reference. The Error Reference has no row with this exact text; the steps follow its 'Invalid File Format' and 'Unsupported media format' rows.
entries.example: Unsupported media type
customerSteps: Check that each media file's format is valid for the platform you are posting to.
Then create the post again with a supported file.
entries.customerWhy: A media file attached to this post is a type that is not supported.
entries.customerAsk: If you would like us to check it for you, reply with the file or files you attached and their type (for example MP4, MOV, JPG, or PNG), and the platform you were posting to.

entries.title: The account credentials were reported as invalid
entries.why: The error says the account credentials are invalid. It does not say which account, or why they are invalid.
nextSteps: Open the failed request in Blotato Logs to see which account the post was sent to and the full error.
Search the Blotato Error Reference for the more specific error text shown there, if any.
The docs give no fix for this exact wording, so do not suggest one to the customer as if it were confirmed. If the Logs do not settle it, escalate with the submission ID and the exact error.
entries.sourceNote: This wording is the example errorMessage for a failed post on the 'REST workflow examples' page. The Error Reference has no row with this text and no fix for it, so the explanation only restates the message and the entry is marked as handled by support.
entries.example: Invalid account credentials
entries.customerWhy: The credentials for the social account used for this post were reported as invalid.
entries.customerAsk: To help them, could you tell me which social account you were posting to, and on which platform?

matchAny: we can only automatically fix videos up to 120 seconds
entries.title: The video is too long for Blotato to convert automatically
entries.why: The video needs changes (such as cropping, resizing, or re-encoding) to fit the destination platform, but Blotato only converts videos up to 120 seconds automatically. The error text names the requirement it could not fix.
nextSteps: Read the error text for the exact requirement that was not met.
Either shorten the video to 120 seconds or less, or export it so it already meets every requirement of the destination platform.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: This video is 185 seconds long, but we can only automatically fix videos up to 120 seconds
customerSteps: Either shorten the video to 120 seconds or less, or export it so it already meets every requirement of the platform you are posting to.
Then create the post again with the new file.
entries.customerWhy: The video needs adjusting to fit the platform (for example cropping, resizing, or re-encoding), and Blotato only does that automatically for videos up to 120 seconds.

matchAny: could not upload media to storage
failed to upload stream to supabase
entries.title: Blotato could not fetch and store the media file
entries.why: Blotato tried to fetch a URL in mediaUrls but could not save it as a media file. The docs say this is almost always because the file is not reachable, not because it is broken. Common causes they list: the URL is not public, it points to a preview page instead of the file itself, the file is larger than the plan allows, or the file is corrupted.
nextSteps: Open each media URL in an incognito/private browser window. It should download the raw file, not show a login or preview page.
Do not use Google Drive or Dropbox share/preview links. Use a direct download link.
Check the file is within your plan's upload size limit.
For a file on your own computer, use Blotato's presigned upload and publish with the publicUrl it returns.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Could not upload media to storage
customerSteps: Open the media link in an incognito/private browser window. It should download the file itself, not show a login or preview page.
If the file is on Google Drive or Dropbox, use a direct download link instead of a share or preview link.
Check the file is within your plan's upload size limit.
For a file on your own computer, upload it to Blotato first (presigned upload) and use the public URL you get back.
Then create the post again.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not download and save the media file from the link in the post. This is almost always because the link is not reachable, rather than the file being broken: for example the link is not public, it opens a preview page instead of the file, or the file is larger than your plan allows.

entries.title: Blotato could not read the media file's details
entries.why: Blotato could not get usable metadata from the media URL. The docs note that a URL opening in your browser does not prove Blotato's servers can fetch it.
nextSteps: Check the media URL returns the file directly, without a login, to a server (not only in your own browser).
Check the file's real container and codecs, and that the upload finished completely.
If the URL starts with claude.ai/artifact/, export the image files from Claude and upload those files instead.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Failed to read media metadata. Is the file accessible and a valid media file?
customerSteps: Make sure the media link returns the file directly, without a login.
If the link starts with claude.ai/artifact/, export the image files from Claude and upload those files instead.
Then create the post again.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not read the details of the media file from its link. A link that opens in your own browser may still be unreachable for our servers.

matchAny: invalid data found when processing input
entries.title: The media file could not be read as valid media
entries.why: Blotato's metadata check could not read its input as valid media. The docs list an error page, an incomplete transfer, or invalid media as possibilities, and say this text alone does not confirm which one.
nextSteps: Check what the media URL actually returns (the file itself, not an error or login page).
Inspect the source file.
Replace or re-encode the file only after you have identified the problem.
entries.example: ClientError: Command failed: ffprobe ... Invalid data found when processing input
customerSteps: Check that the media link returns the media file itself, not an error page.
Inspect the source file, and replace or re-export it only once you have found what is wrong with it.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not read the file behind the media link as valid media. That can happen when the link returns an error page, the file transfer was incomplete, or the file itself is not valid media.

entries.title: Media conversion did not finish
entries.why: The conversion did not finish. The docs say this message alone does not identify the cause, and that Blotato also returns it when the source download fails or comes back empty.
nextSteps: Inspect the source media URL and the exact processing error in Blotato Logs.
Check the file's metadata against the destination platform's requirements.
Check the original submission's status before retrying.
entries.example: Media conversion failed
customerSteps: Check that the source media link opens the file.
Check the file against the requirements of the platform you are posting to.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not finish converting the media. This also happens when the file cannot be downloaded from its link, or the download comes back empty.

entries.title: Blotato could not fetch the media URL
entries.why: Fetching the media URL did not return something Blotato could read. The docs say the unexpected character in this error does not establish the full response or the cause.
nextSteps: Check the media URL is accessible, has not expired, and returns actual media content.
If the file was uploaded first, confirm the upload completed.
Check the original submission's status before submitting again.
entries.example: Failed to fetch media URL: char '<' is not expected.:1:1
customerSteps: Check that the media link is accessible, has not expired, and returns actual media content.
If the file was uploaded first, make sure that upload finished.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato could not fetch usable media from the link in the post.

entries.title: A URL in the request was empty
entries.why: The URL that was submitted is empty.
nextSteps: Look at the step before this one in your workflow, and at the field that was mapped into the request.
If the URL comes from a generated visual, confirm the visual finished and use the mediaUrl or imageUrls it returned.
Do not just add a longer fixed wait; check the status and errors of the earlier step.
entries.example: URL is empty
customerSteps: Look at the step before this one in your workflow, and at the field that feeds the URL into the post.
If the URL comes from a generated visual, make sure the visual has finished and use the media URL it returned.
entries.customerWhy: The media URL sent with this post was empty.

entries.title: The media URL was missing
entries.why: The docs explain this as the video not being finished when the post was sent.
nextSteps: Wait until the video has finished generating before publishing.
Check that you have AI credits (Settings > Billing, or GET /v2/credits).
entries.example: mediaURL is null or empty
customerSteps: Wait until the video has finished generating before publishing.
Check that you have AI credits left (Settings > Billing).
entries.customerWhy: The media URL was missing, which means the video had not finished generating when the post was sent.

entries.title: A media-processing result was missing
entries.why: The publishing queue did not receive one usable media-processing result for every media URL in the post.
nextSteps: If the media came from a generated visual, confirm that job reached "done".
Confirm every value in mediaUrls is a public file URL.
Retry the post once. If the same error returns, escalate to the technical team with the request ID.
Reconnect a social account only if Blotato Logs show a separate authentication error.
entries.example: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mediaUrl')
customerSteps: If the media came from a generated visual, confirm that it finished ("done").
Confirm every media URL in the post is a public file URL.
Then try the post once more.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato did not get a usable processing result for every media file in the post.

entries.title: The social platform did not return a response
entries.why: The social platform did not return a response. The docs say this is usually a temporary issue.
nextSteps: Wait a few minutes, then retry (in the web app: Posts > Failed).
If the error persists, check that the media file is in a format the platform supports.
entries.example: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')
customerSteps: Wait a few minutes, then retry the post (in the web app: Posts > Failed).
If it keeps happening, check that your media file is in a format the platform supports.
entries.customerWhy: The social platform did not send back a response. This is usually temporary.

entries.title: The file format is not valid for the platform
entries.why: The file format does not meet the destination platform's requirements.
nextSteps: Check the file format against the destination platform's media requirements.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Invalid File Format
customerSteps: Check that your file format is valid for the platform you are posting to.
Then create the post again with a supported file.
entries.customerWhy: The file format is not valid for the platform you posted to.

entries.title: The video's dimensions are not supported by the platform
entries.why: The destination platform does not support the video's dimensions.
nextSteps: Export the video in dimensions the platform accepts. For a portrait Instagram Reel, the docs name 1080 x 1920 or 720 x 1280 as compatible presets.
Videos longer than 120 seconds are not resized automatically, so resize those before uploading.
Then submit a corrected post.
entries.example: Invalid Video Dimensions
customerSteps: Export the video in dimensions the platform supports. For a portrait Instagram Reel, 1080 x 1920 or 720 x 1280 works.
A video longer than 120 seconds is not resized automatically, so resize it before uploading.
entries.customerWhy: The platform does not support the video's dimensions.

matchAny: the aspect ratio is not supported
entries.title: The video's aspect ratio is not supported by the platform
entries.why: The destination platform does not support the video's aspect ratio.
nextSteps: Check the platform's requirements and export the video in a supported aspect ratio.
Then submit a corrected post.
entries.example: The aspect ratio is not supported
customerSteps: Check the platform's requirements and export the video in a supported aspect ratio.
entries.customerWhy: The platform does not support the video's aspect ratio.

entries.title: The media file is larger than your plan allows
entries.why: The media file is larger than the upload size limit of your Blotato plan.
nextSteps: Compress or trim the file so it is under the limit named in the error.
Or upgrade your plan to raise the limit.
entries.example: File exceeds the maximum upload size (100 MB) for your plan. Upload a smaller file, or upgrade your plan to increase your max upload size.
customerSteps: Compress or trim the file so it is under the limit, or upgrade your plan to raise the limit.
entries.customerWhy: The media file is larger than the upload limit of your Blotato plan.

matchAny: please reduce the amount of data you're asking for
entries.title: Facebook asked to reduce the amount of data
entries.why: The docs say this message does not establish an outage, memory exhaustion, or a follower-count threshold, so the cause is not known from the text alone. They also warn that the error does not prove nothing was published.
nextSteps: Check the Facebook Page and the original submission before retrying.
Keep the exact response and request ID.
If it is still unclear, escalate to the technical team with that evidence.

links.label: Find a post's outcome before retrying

entries.example: Could not upload video to Facebook: Please reduce the amount of data you're asking for, then retry your request
customerSteps: Before trying again, check your Facebook Page to see whether the post went out.
entries.customerWhy: Facebook sent back this message, but the message alone does not tell us the reason. It is also possible that the post went out anyway.

entries.title: The video could not be uploaded to the platform
entries.why: Each platform has its own requirements for video uploads, and the docs point to those requirements for this error.
nextSteps: Check the video against the destination platform's video requirements.
Then submit a corrected post. An unchanged retry often fails for the same reason.
entries.example: Post failed to publish. Could not upload video
customerSteps: Check that your video follows the requirements of the platform you are posting to.
entries.customerWhy: The video could not be uploaded to the platform. Each platform has its own requirements for video uploads.

entries.title: The platform rejected the media
entries.why: The platform rejected the media Blotato tried to upload. The docs say this is not a rate-limit or credits problem, and that retrying the same media without changes will not help. Common causes they list: the media does not meet the platform's format or size specs, or the account connection is stale.
nextSteps: Open the failed post in Posts > Failed or in Blotato Logs to read the exact error for this post.
Check the media against the platform's format and size requirements.
If the media is fine, reconnect the account in Accounts and retry.
If several platforms show this at once, check each post's error separately; the cause can differ per platform.
entries.example: Could not upload media to Twitter
customerSteps: Open the failed post under Posts > Failed to read the exact error for it.
Check the media against the platform's format and size requirements.
If the media is fine, reconnect the account under Accounts, then retry.
entries.customerWhy: The platform did not accept the media in your post, so sending the same file again without changes will not help. This has nothing to do with how often you post or with your credits. Usually the file does not meet the platform's format or size requirements, or the account connection needs to be refreshed.

matchAny: authorization failed - please check your credentials
entries.title: The Blotato API key was not accepted
entries.why: Blotato did not accept the API key used for the request.
nextSteps: Double-check the Blotato API key: copy it again in full, with no extra spaces.
In n8n or Make, the official Blotato nodes avoid copying keys and IDs by hand.
entries.example: Authorization failed - please check your credentials
customerSteps: Double-check the Blotato API key used in your workflow: copy it again in full, with no extra spaces.
If you use n8n or Make, the official Blotato nodes save you from copying keys and IDs by hand.
entries.customerWhy: The Blotato API key used for the request was not accepted.

matchAny: the service is receiving too many requests from you
entries.title: Blotato's API rate limit was exceeded
entries.why: Too many requests were sent to Blotato in a short time. The docs list 30 requests per minute each for Upload Media and Publish Post.
nextSteps: Slow the workflow down so it stays under the limit.
Check whether the post was created before sending it again, to avoid a duplicate.
entries.example: The service is receiving too many requests from you
customerSteps: Slow your workflow down: publishing posts and uploading media are each limited to 30 requests per minute.
entries.customerWhy: Too many requests were sent to Blotato in a short time.

entries.title: The account ID was not found
entries.why: The account ID in the request does not match the Blotato user and platform. The docs list these causes: the ID does not belong to the API key that was used, the account was disconnected, or the ID is from another platform. For LinkedIn company pages, a common mistake is passing the pageId where the accountId is expected.
nextSteps: List your accounts again with the same API key (GET /v2/users/me/accounts) and use an ID from that list.
For LinkedIn or Facebook Pages, put the account ID in post.accountId and the Page ID in post.target.pageId.
Do not rely on IDs saved earlier in a dropdown or copied from an old lookup; they may no longer be current.
entries.example: Account 98432 not found
customerSteps: List your connected accounts again with the same API key or connection, and use an account ID from that list.
For a LinkedIn company page or Facebook Page, send the account ID as the account and the Page ID as the page; they are two different IDs.
entries.customerWhy: The account ID in the request was not found for your Blotato user and that platform. This happens when the ID belongs to a different API key, the account was disconnected, or the ID is from another platform. With LinkedIn company pages, a common mix-up is sending the Page ID where the account ID belongs.

matchAny: the user has not authorized application
entries.title: The Instagram/Facebook connection is no longer authorized
entries.why: The Meta access token for this account is no longer valid. The docs say tokens go stale when they expire, when they are revoked (for example after a password change or security refresh), or when the Blotato app was removed from Business Integrations.
nextSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts and click Reconnect on this account.
In the Meta popup, approve access with both the Instagram account and its linked Facebook Page checked.
After reconnecting, submit the post again.
entries.example: The user has not authorized application
customerSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts and click Reconnect on this account.
In the Meta popup, approve access with both the Instagram account and its linked Facebook Page checked.
Then submit the post again.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato's access to this Instagram/Facebook account is no longer valid. That happens when the access expires, is revoked (for example after a password change or a security refresh), or the Blotato app was removed from Business Integrations.

matchAny: the user is not a confirmed user
entries.title: Instagram says the account session is not confirmed
entries.why: This error comes from Instagram/Meta: the Instagram account's session is not confirmed.
nextSteps: Log into the Instagram account in a browser and complete any pending prompts (email or phone confirmation, security checks, updated terms).
Reconnect the account in Blotato: disconnect it, then reconnect using an incognito browser logged into only that Instagram account.
Check the account is a Professional or Business account; the docs say personal accounts have problems with third-party publishing.
entries.example: Could not publish on Instagram: Error validating access token: Sessions for the user are not allowed because the user is not a confirmed user
customerSteps: Log into the Instagram account in a browser and complete any pending prompts (email or phone confirmation, security checks, updated terms).
In Blotato, disconnect the account and reconnect it using an incognito browser logged into only that Instagram account.
Check that it is a Professional or Business account.
entries.customerWhy: This error comes from Instagram/Meta: the session for the Instagram account is not confirmed.

entries.title: An authorization has expired (invalid_grant)
entries.why: The docs list invalid_grant in two places: an expired Instagram/Meta authorization token on a connected social account, and an expired Blotato MCP connection inside Claude. For a post sent through the REST API, the first one is the one that involves a social account.
nextSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts, find the Instagram account, and click Reconnect. Then retry.
If you were using Blotato through Claude (MCP) instead, remove and re-add the Blotato connector in Claude and approve access again.
The docs note this error often causes follow-on "mediaUrl" errors; fix the authorization first.
entries.example: invalid_grant
customerSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts, find the Instagram account, and click Reconnect. Then retry.
If you use Blotato through Claude instead, remove and re-add the Blotato connector in Claude and approve access again.
entries.customerWhy: An authorization has expired. This is the Instagram/Meta connection of the social account or, if you use Blotato through Claude, the Blotato connection inside Claude.

entries.title: The social account needs to be reconnected
entries.why: The account's authorization token expired, or the account needs some other manual reconnect or confirmation.
nextSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts and click Reconnect on this account.
After reconnecting, submit the post again.
entries.example: Account requires reconnect
customerSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts and click Reconnect on this account.
Then retry the post.
entries.customerWhy: The authorization for this social account has expired, or the account needs to be reconnected or confirmed manually.

entries.title: Facebook says the Page permissions are missing
entries.why: Facebook requires the pages_read_engagement and pages_manage_posts permissions, held by someone with enough admin rights on the Page. The docs also note Blotato publishes to Pages, not to Groups or personal profiles.
nextSteps: Confirm the Facebook identity you connected has publishing access to the Page.
Reconnect that identity in Accounts and select the required Page and permissions.
Do not remove the Blotato integration from Facebook as a routine step.
entries.example: Error posting to Facebook: (#200) requires pages_read_engagement and pages_manage_posts permission
customerSteps: Confirm the Facebook login you connected has publishing access to the Page.
Reconnect that Facebook login under Accounts, and select the Page and the requested permissions.
entries.customerWhy: Facebook requires permission to read and publish on the Page, from someone with enough admin rights on it. Blotato publishes to Pages, not to Groups or personal profiles.

matchAny: create a tweet with duplicate content
entries.title: X (Twitter) rejected the post as a duplicate
entries.why: X rejects a post whose text is identical to a previous tweet on the same account.
nextSteps: Check the X account first: the earlier, identical tweet may already be live.
If you still want to post, change the caption text (even slightly) before posting again.
If the same post was scheduled twice by accident, delete the duplicate in Posts > Scheduled.
entries.example: You are not allowed to create a Tweet with duplicate content
customerSteps: Change the caption text (even slightly) before posting again.
If the same post was scheduled twice by accident, delete the duplicate under Posts > Scheduled.
entries.customerWhy: X (Twitter) rejects a post whose text is identical to an earlier tweet on the same account.

matchAny: not allowed to post a video longer than 2 minutes
entries.title: X (Twitter) rejected the video's length for this account
entries.why: X rejected the video's duration for the connected account. The docs say Blotato passes X videos through without converting them, so Blotato's 120-second conversion limit is not the cause here, and that an X Premium subscription does not guarantee acceptance.
nextSteps: Check the X account's API publishing restrictions and X's file requirements.
Shorten the video if the account is not allowed longer videos, then submit a corrected post.
entries.example: This user is not allowed to post a video longer than 2 minutes
customerSteps: Check your X account's publishing restrictions and X's video file requirements.
entries.customerWhy: X (Twitter) rejected the video's length for this account. Blotato sends X videos as they are, without converting them, and an X Premium subscription does not guarantee that longer videos are accepted.

matchAny: you are not permitted to perform this action
entries.title: X (Twitter) did not permit this action
entries.why: The docs explain this X error as an expired authorization or changed permissions on the connected account.
nextSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts, find the X (Twitter) account, and click Reconnect.
Re-authorize the app when X asks.
After reconnecting, submit the post again.
entries.example: You are not permitted to perform this action
customerSteps: In Blotato, go to Accounts, find your X (Twitter) account, and click Reconnect.
Re-authorize the app when X asks, then retry the post.
entries.customerWhy: The authorization for your X (Twitter) account has expired, or its permissions changed.

matchAny: unique accounts for the last 24 hours
entries.title: The Starter plan's TikTok account limit was reached
entries.why: This is a posting limit on the Starter plan, not a limit on connected accounts: Blotato counts the distinct TikTok accounts that had successful posts in the last rolling 24 hours, and allows 3. Posting again to one of those accounts does not use another slot.
nextSteps: Wait until one of the earlier accounts leaves the 24-hour window, or post to one of the accounts already used.
Or upgrade the plan to remove this limit.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 3 unique accounts for the last 24 hours. Please upgrade your plan to add more.
customerSteps: Wait until one of the 3 TikTok accounts you posted to leaves the 24-hour window, or post to one of those same accounts.
Or upgrade your plan to remove this limit.
entries.customerWhy: On the Starter plan you can post to 3 different TikTok accounts within any 24 hours. This is a posting limit, not a limit on connected accounts, and posting again to one of those 3 accounts is still allowed.

entries.matchRegex: posts for the last 24 hours for this account.*\byoutube\b|\byoutube\b.*posts for the last 24 hours for this account
entries.title: The YouTube channel reached its 24-hour posting limit
entries.why: Blotato enforces 10 posts per YouTube channel per rolling 24 hours on Starter, or 25 on Creator and Agency. YouTube's own restrictions are separate.
nextSteps: Have the customer check the original outcome before retrying or uploading manually, to avoid a duplicate.
Then wait for earlier successful posts to leave the 24-hour window.
entries.customerWhy: On the Starter plan, Blotato allows 10 posts per YouTube channel in any 24 hours (25 on Creator and Agency), and this channel has reached that limit. YouTube's own limits apply separately.
customerSteps: Before trying again or uploading the video manually, check whether the original post already went out on YouTube, so it does not appear twice.
Then wait until earlier posts drop out of the 24-hour window before posting to this channel again.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 10 posts for the last 24 hours for this account (YouTube)
entries.sourceNote: The Error Reference lists this error with "(YouTube)" after it. It is not clear whether the platform name is part of the real error message; when it is not, the general entry posting-limit-24h is used instead.

entries.matchRegex: posts for the last 24 hours for this account.*\bfacebook\b|\bfacebook\b.*posts for the last 24 hours for this account
entries.title: The Facebook Page reached its 24-hour posting limit
entries.why: Facebook publishing is limited to 25 posts per 24 hours per Page. Each Page has its own independent limit. (The docs say "per 24 hours" here, not "rolling".)
nextSteps: Wait 24 hours and try again, or publish to a different Page.
entries.customerWhy: Facebook publishing is limited to 25 posts per 24 hours for each Page, and this Page has reached that limit.
customerSteps: Wait 24 hours, then try again.
Or publish to a different Page, since each Page has its own limit.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 25 posts for the last 24 hours for this account (Facebook)
entries.sourceNote: The Error Reference lists this error with "(Facebook)" after it. It is not clear whether the platform name is part of the real error message; when it is not, the general entry posting-limit-24h is used instead.

entries.matchRegex: posts for the last 24 hours for this account.*\blinkedin\b|\blinkedin\b.*posts for the last 24 hours for this account
entries.title: The LinkedIn profile or Page reached its 24-hour posting limit
entries.why: LinkedIn publishing is limited to 50 posts per 24 hours per profile and per company Page. Each has its own independent limit. (The docs say "per 24 hours" here, not "rolling".)
nextSteps: Wait 24 hours and try again, or publish to a different profile or company Page.
entries.customerWhy: LinkedIn publishing is limited to 50 posts per 24 hours for each profile and each company Page, and this one has reached that limit.
customerSteps: Wait 24 hours, then try again.
Or publish to a different profile or company Page, since each has its own limit.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 50 posts for the last 24 hours for this account (LinkedIn)
entries.sourceNote: The Error Reference lists this error with "(LinkedIn)" after it. It is not clear whether the platform name is part of the real error message; when it is not, the general entry posting-limit-24h is used instead.

entries.matchRegex: posts for the last 24 hours for this account.*\bslack\b|\bslack\b.*posts for the last 24 hours for this account
entries.title: The Slack channel reached its 24-hour posting limit
entries.why: Blotato limits each Slack channel to 100 posts per rolling 24 hours, on every plan, so upgrading does not raise it. Each channel has its own limit.
nextSteps: Wait for earlier posts to leave the 24-hour window, or publish to another channel.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato allows 100 posts per Slack channel in any 24 hours, on every plan, and this channel has reached that limit. Upgrading the plan does not raise it.
customerSteps: Wait until earlier posts drop out of the 24-hour window, then post again.
Or publish to another channel, since each channel has its own limit.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 100 posts for the last 24 hours for this account (Slack)
entries.sourceNote: The Error Reference lists this error with "(Slack)" after it. It is not clear whether the platform name is part of the real error message; when it is not, the general entry posting-limit-24h is used instead.

matchAny: posts for the last 24 hours for this account
entries.title: A 24-hour posting limit was reached
entries.why: This destination reached a posting limit for a 24-hour period; the number in the error is the limit that applied. The status response does not say which platform it was, and the same number can belong to several platforms (Platform Posting Limits: TikTok 25 per account, with an older Starter message that still says 10; Instagram 50 per day; Pinterest 10, 20, or 50; Facebook 25 per Page; LinkedIn 50 per profile or Page; YouTube 10 on Starter or 25; Slack 100 per channel). YouTube, Slack, TikTok, and Pinterest count a rolling 24 hours; for Facebook and LinkedIn the docs say "per 24 hours".
nextSteps: Find out which platform and destination the post was for (Blotato Posts or Logs), then use that platform's row in the Error Reference.
Ask the customer to check whether the original post already went out before posting again, to avoid a duplicate.
Do not give the customer a list of platform limits unless you know which platform this was.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of 25 posts for the last 24 hours for this account
customerSteps: Before trying again, check whether the original post already went out, so it does not appear twice.
Then wait 24 hours before posting to this account again.
entries.customerWhy: This account has reached its posting limit for a 24-hour period. The number in the message above is the limit that applied.
entries.sourceNote: General entry for the 24-hour limit when the error does not name a platform this catalog has a row for (YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack). It deliberately gives the customer no list of platform limits, because the platform is unknown and the same number can belong to several platforms (for example TikTok).

entries.title: Your plan's limit of scheduled posts was reached
entries.why: The number of queued scheduled posts reached your plan's limit.
nextSteps: Delete some upcoming posts in Posts > Scheduled, or upgrade your plan.
Then schedule the post again.
entries.example: You have reached the maximum number of scheduled posts (100) for your plan. Please remove some scheduled posts or upgrade your plan.
customerSteps: Delete some upcoming posts under Posts > Scheduled, or upgrade your plan.
entries.customerWhy: You have reached the number of scheduled posts your plan allows.

entries.customerWhy: The scheduled time is more than 9 months in the future.

entries.title: No free calendar slot was found
entries.why: Blotato found no available matching slot in its search window. This applies when scheduling to the "next free slot".
nextSteps: Open the weekly schedule in Blotato and check that slots exist for this platform and account (or Page/channel) and still have free times.
Add a slot if needed, or schedule the post for an exact time instead; exact-time scheduling does not need slots.
Do not simply remove the scheduling fields: a request without them publishes immediately.
entries.example: Could not schedule post: No available slot time found in the next 9 months
customerSteps: Open your weekly schedule in Blotato and check that slots exist for this platform and account, with free times.
Add a slot if needed, or schedule the post for an exact time instead; that does not need slots.
Please do not just remove the scheduling settings: a post without them is published immediately.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato looked for the next free slot in your posting schedule and did not find one.

Check that your YouTube account is verified.

entries.title: The platform is rate-limiting this account
entries.why: The platform is limiting publishing for the connected account. The docs describe this for repeated YouTube or LinkedIn failures.
nextSteps: Wait an hour, then retry from Posts > Failed.
If posts keep failing with this error after waiting, reconnect the social account in Accounts and retry; the docs say a stale connection token can keep triggering the limiter.
entries.example: Exceeded rate limits
customerSteps: Wait an hour, then retry the post from Posts > Failed.
If it keeps failing with this error after waiting, reconnect the social account under Accounts, then retry.
entries.customerWhy: The platform is limiting how often this account can publish.

entries.title: The post text is too long for the platform
entries.why: The text is longer than the destination platform (or the connected X account) allows. The docs note that emoji and full-width characters count as 2.
nextSteps: Shorten the text, and any additional posts in the thread that the error names.
Then submit the corrected post.
entries.example: Text length exceeds the character limit of 280 characters for platform twitter
customerSteps: Shorten the text (and any additional posts in the thread that the error names). Emoji and full-width characters count as 2.
Then submit the post again.
entries.customerWhy: The text is longer than the platform allows.

entries.title: The post has more than 5 hashtags
entries.why: This is a Blotato guardrail, not an Instagram rule. Blotato caps posts at 5 hashtags on purpose.
nextSteps: Trim the caption to 5 hashtags or fewer.
Then publish the corrected post.
entries.example: Instagram allows a maximum of 5 hashtags per post
customerSteps: Trim the caption to 5 hashtags or fewer, then publish again.
entries.customerWhy: Instagram itself allows more hashtags, but Blotato limits posts to 5 on purpose, because more than 5 hashtags reduces reach on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.

entries.title: The number of attachments does not fit an Instagram carousel
entries.why: Instagram says the post has too few or too many attachments to be a carousel. Through the API, Instagram supports at most 10 images or videos per carousel.
nextSteps: Change the number of media files so it fits a carousel (no more than 10).
Then submit the corrected post.
entries.example: Could not publish on Instagram: Unsupported post type. The post has too little or too many attachments to qualify as a carousel
customerSteps: Use no more than 10 images or videos in the carousel, then submit the post again.
entries.customerWhy: Instagram did not accept the number of images or videos as a carousel. Through Blotato, a carousel can have at most 10.

entries.title: Instagram returned a temporary error
entries.why: Instagram returned a temporary error while Blotato was publishing. Blotato already retried on its own before reporting this.
nextSteps: Wait a few minutes, then retry the post from Posts > Failed.
The error message ends with a reference ID. Include it if you escalate to the technical team because the post keeps failing.
entries.example: Instagram encountered a temporary error while publishing your post. Please try again in a few minutes.
customerSteps: Wait a few minutes, then retry the post from Posts > Failed.
If it keeps failing, reply with the reference ID at the end of the error message.
entries.customerWhy: Instagram returned a temporary error while the post was being published. Blotato already retried automatically before reporting it.

entries.why: Blotato used up its waiting and retry attempts while Instagram still reported the media as not ready. The docs warn that a timeout alone is not proof that nothing was posted.
nextSteps: Keep the reference ID from the error message.
Check the Instagram account and the original post's status before retrying.
If nothing was posted, retry after a delay.

If it is not there, try the post again after a few minutes.
If it keeps failing, reply with the reference ID from the error message.
entries.customerWhy: Instagram was still processing the media when Blotato ran out of retries. It is possible that the post went out anyway.

entries.example: Error posting to Instagram: An internal server error occurred
customerSteps: Wait a few hours, then retry the post from Posts > Failed.

Leave more time between posts.

Shorten the caption.
Leave more time between posts.

Check that the media URL is publicly accessible (open it in an incognito window).
Reduce hashtags and caption length, and leave more time between posts.
If it still fails after reconnecting, reply with the reqId from the error message.

Space your posts out instead of retrying quickly.

Post on the Threads account manually for a few days before connecting it to Blotato.

Escalate to the technical team, or follow retry guidance they have confirmed.

Then submit the post again.

Then submit the post again.

nextSteps: Wait 15 to 30 minutes, then retry.
If the error persists, reconnect the TikTok account in Accounts.

customerSteps: Wait 15 to 30 minutes, then retry.
If the error persists, reconnect your TikTok account under Accounts.

nextSteps: Retry after a few minutes.
If it keeps failing, reconnect the TikTok account in Accounts.

If it keeps failing, reconnect your TikTok account under Accounts.

nextSteps: Check the TikTok account before submitting again, in case the post went out.
Then escalate to the technical team with the full error and reference IDs.
entries.example: Failed to publish TikTok post after 3 retries (Unknown error reason)
customerSteps: Please also check your TikTok account, in case the post did go out.
entries.customerWhy: Blotato tried to publish the post several times, and TikTok did not accept it. TikTok gave a reason that Blotato cannot describe yet. That does not mean there was an outage or a problem with your credits.

matchAny: update their tiktok to the latest version
entries.title: TikTok asked for the app to be updated (photo posts)
entries.why: This error comes from TikTok on image and carousel posts. The docs say it appears even when the TikTok app is already up to date.
nextSteps: On the phone connected to that TikTok account: update the app, open it and log in, force close, reopen, then clear the cache under Settings and privacy > Free up space.
Retry from Posts > Failed.
If it persists, choose Reconnect for the TikTok account in Accounts.
If it still returns, escalate to the technical team so the TikTok account can be removed and then connected fresh.
entries.example: Error uploading images to TikTok: Please notice the user to update their TikTok to the latest version to enable this functionality
customerSteps: On the phone connected to that TikTok account: update the TikTok app, open it and log in, force close it, reopen it, then go to Profile > Settings and privacy > Free up space and clear the cache.
Retry the post from Posts > Failed.
If it persists, choose Reconnect for the TikTok account under Accounts.
entries.customerWhy: This error comes from TikTok on image and carousel posts. It can appear even when the TikTok app is already up to date.

entries.title: TikTok does not support the picture's size
entries.why: TikTok rejected the image's size. The docs note that Blotato tries to normalize images, but a successful upload does not prove TikTok accepted the image.
nextSteps: Check the image's format, dimensions, and file size.
Use a JPEG export, for example 1080 x 1920 for portrait images, at no more than 20 MB.
Then submit a corrected post.
entries.example: Unsupported picture size
customerSteps: Export the image as a JPEG, for example 1080 x 1920 for a portrait image, at no more than 20 MB.
Then submit the post again.
entries.customerWhy: TikTok did not accept the size of the image.

entries.title: TikTok brand fields are missing from the request
entries.why: Every TikTok post sent through the REST API (including the n8n and Make nodes) must include both isYourBrand and isBrandedContent. There is no default.
nextSteps: Add both fields inside the target object (not content), even when both are false.
Set isYourBrand to true when the post promotes your own brand, and isBrandedContent to true for a paid partnership.
Then submit the corrected post.
entries.example: body.post.target must have required property 'isYourBrand' or 'isBrandedContent'
customerSteps: Add both isYourBrand and isBrandedContent inside the target object of the request, even when both are false.
Set isYourBrand to true when the post promotes your own brand, and isBrandedContent to true for a paid partnership.
entries.customerWhy: Every TikTok post sent through the API must state whether it promotes your own brand and whether it is branded content. Both settings are required, and there is no default.

nextSteps: As a workaround, the docs suggest adding parameters to the link (for example ?ref=pin&v=111) so Pinterest treats it as a new URL.
Then submit the pin again.
entries.example: Sorry! This site doesn't allow you to save Pins.
customerSteps: As a workaround, add parameters to your link (for example ?ref=pin&v=111) so Pinterest sees it as a new URL that gets past the filter, then submit the pin again.
entries.customerWhy: This error comes from Pinterest. The two common causes are that the website has asked not to be pinned, or that Pinterest's blocklist flagged the link (often by mistake).

matchAny: pinterest api access is temporarily restricted to verified accounts
entries.title: Pinterest restricts API access for this account
entries.why: Pinterest restricts API access to verified accounts. An account is verified automatically when it is reconnected after reaching 100+ monthly views. The Error Reference says a new account MUST be warmed up for 2 weeks first; other help pages say 1-2 weeks (Pinterest troubleshooting) or 2-3 weeks (Social accounts).
nextSteps: Ask the customer to warm the account up for 2 weeks (per the Error Reference): 1 pin per day manually, then 2, then 3, and so on.
Once the account has 100+ monthly views, they reconnect it under Accounts and retry; verification is automatic.
If the account already has 100+ monthly views, skip the warm-up and have them reconnect now.
entries.example: Pinterest API access is temporarily restricted to verified accounts only
customerSteps: Warm the account up for 2 weeks before connecting it to Blotato again: post manually, starting with 1 pin per day, then 2, then 3, and so on. Skipping the warm-up often gets the account shadowbanned or flagged by Pinterest.
Once the account has 100+ monthly views, go to Accounts, click Reconnect on the Pinterest account, and retry.
If your account already has 100+ monthly views, you can skip the warm-up and reconnect now.
entries.customerWhy: Pinterest is limiting access for posting tools like Blotato to verified accounts, and this account still looks new. An account becomes verified automatically when you reconnect it after it reaches 100+ monthly views.

entries.title: Pinterest rejected the pin without a readable reason
